directAnswer: Pope John XXII was Jacques Duèze of Cahors, elected at Lyon on 7 August 1316 at about seventy-two, who reigned at Avignon until 4 December 1334. A tireless administrator, he reorganized papal finances, canonized Thomas Aquinas, and condemned the Franciscan teaching that Christ and the apostles owned nothing. He also stirred controversy with sermons on the beatific vision, which he retracted before his death.

paras: Jacques Duèze was born at Cahors in southern France and studied law. He served the Angevin kings of Naples as chancellor, became bishop of Fréjus and then of Avignon, and was created a cardinal by Clement V. After Clement's death the cardinals were divided for more than two years until they were assembled at Lyon in 1316 and chose him.
Many expected a brief transitional reign from a man in his seventies. Instead he governed for eighteen years and became one of the most energetic popes of the Middle Ages.

John reorganized the papal administration and finances, expanding the system of reserved benefices and fees that funded the curia. He created new dioceses in southern France and elsewhere and organized the papal court at Avignon. He also promulgated the Clementines, the canonical collection of his predecessor, in 1317, and his own decrees circulated as the Extravagantes.
In 1323 he canonized Thomas Aquinas. In 1329 he condemned a series of propositions drawn from the writings of the Dominican Meister Eckhart in the bull In agro dominico.

sections.h2: Franciscan Poverty, Ockham and Louis of Bavaria
paras: John confronted the Spiritual Franciscans and then the whole order over poverty. In 1322 he renounced papal ownership of Franciscan goods, undermining the arrangement set by Nicholas III, and in the bull Cum inter nonnullos of 1323 he declared it heretical to assert that Christ and the apostles had owned nothing at all.

The minister general Michael of Cesena and the philosopher William of Ockham fled to the court of Louis of Bavaria, whom John refused to recognize as emperor. Ockham wrote extensively against the pope's authority. Louis was crowned in Rome in 1328 by lay representatives and set up an antipope, Nicholas V, who submitted to John in 1330.

From 1331 John preached that the souls of the blessed would not see God face to face until after the Last Judgment, enjoying in the meantime only the vision of Christ's humanity. He presented this as his opinion as a theologian rather than as a definition, but it met strong opposition from theologians in Paris and elsewhere.

Shortly before his death, John declared that the purified souls of the faithful departed see the divine essence clearly, so far as their state allows, and submitted his views to the judgment of the Church. He died at Avignon on 4 December 1334. His successor, Benedict XII, settled the question with the constitution Benedictus Deus.

keyFacts: Born Jacques Duèze at Cahors; former bishop of Avignon
Elected at Lyon in 1316 after a vacancy of more than two years
Reigned eighteen years at Avignon and reorganized papal finances
Condemned the doctrine of the absolute poverty of Christ in Cum inter nonnullos (1323)
Retracted his beatific vision opinion before dying on 4 December 1334

faqs.question: Did Pope John XXII teach heresy about heaven?
faqs.answer: He preached, as a private theological opinion, that the saved would not see God fully until the Last Judgment. It was never defined, he retracted it before his death in 1334, and Benedict XII's Benedictus Deus defined the opposite.

faqs.question: Why did William of Ockham oppose John XXII?
faqs.answer: John rejected the Franciscan claim that Christ and the apostles owned nothing. Ockham, siding with the Franciscan minister general Michael of Cesena, fled to Louis of Bavaria and wrote against the pope's authority.

faqs.question: Which saint did John XXII canonize?
faqs.answer: He canonized St. Thomas Aquinas in 1323, less than fifty years after the Dominican theologian's death.
